title: Descent to the whole equivariant function algebra
statement: Let R and H be commutative rings in one universe u, g an element of R, and iota:R -> H a ring homomorphism. Let C be a commutative H-algebra which is a domain, finite and faithfully flat over H. Let G be a finite group and rho:G -> End_H(C) satisfy rho(1)=id and rho(ab)=rho(a) composed with rho(b). Set h=algebraMap(H,C)(iota(g)), assume h is nonzero, and put V=D(h) in Spec C and q:Spec C -> Spec H. Assume V -> Spec H is etale. Assume that for every field Omega in universe u and ring maps a,b:C -> Omega agreeing on H, if a(h) is nonzero then there exists a unique zeta in G with a composed with rho(zeta)=b. Let j:Y -> D(g) in Spec R be finite etale and let p:Y -> Spec R be its composite with the open inclusion. Let d be a natural number, t:T -> Spec R a morphism, and k:V -> T a morphism satisfying t composed with k=(Spec iota) composed with q restricted to V. Suppose delta:Y times_(Spec R) T -> coproduct_(Fin d) T is an isomorphism over T. Then there exists a group homomorphism alpha:G -> Perm(Fin d) such that, for A=affineTorsorEquivariantAlgebra(H,C,G,rho,d,alpha) [def-sbc-affine-torsor-equivariant-algebra], Y times_(Spec R) Spec H is isomorphic over Spec H to D(algebraMap(H,A)(iota(g))) in Spec A. The structural map of this principal open is induced by algebraMap(H,A).

proof.text:
Proof: put h=ι(g). Faithful flatness makes D(h) in Spec C a surjective finite
flat cover of D(h) in Spec H. It is etale by assumption, and the unique-rotation
hypothesis makes the map from G copies of this cover to its self-fibre-product
an isomorphism: both are finite etale and it is bijective on geometric fibres.
Pull δ back along k to split Y over D(h) in Spec C into d components. This
principal open is nonempty and connected since C is a domain and h is nonzero.
The descent datum therefore permutes the components, and the cocycle law gives
α : G →* Perm(Fin d), with the convention ρ a (f i)=f(α a i).
Affine faithfully flat descent identifies the descended algebra with these
equivariant functions in C[1/h]. They equal the localization of the explicitly
constructed equivariant algebra in C: clear denominators simultaneously in the
finite product, and use injectivity of C → C[1/h] to remove every factor of h
from the equivariance equations. All algebra maps fix H, so the identification
is in Over(Spec H). If d=0 both sides are empty. No orbit representatives,
stabilizers, or product of fixed rings are asserted by this step.
